name: Prof. Flora Josiane Chadare
bio:
Dr. Flora Josiane Chadare is the representative of Benin on the WASCAL Governing Board. She holds a PhD in Food Science, Technology, and Nutrition, along with master’s degrees in Nutrition and Food Science, and Food Technology, a diploma in Agricultural Engineering (Nutrition and Food Science option), and a diploma in General Agronomy.

She is a Senior Lecturer in Nutrition and Food Science (CAMES) and the Director of the Laboratory of Food and Bioresource Science and Technology and Human Nutrition at the National University of Agriculture (Benin). Dr. Chadare coordinates the “Nutrition and Food Science” PhD programme and serves as the Director of the School of Science and Technology for the Processing and Conservation of Agricultural Products (ESTCTPA/UNA). She is also the Coordinator of continuing vocational training at ESTCTPA.

Before joining the National University, she was the Director of the National and International Cooperation Department at the Ecole Nationale des Sciences et Techniques de Conservation. She has held roles such as Monitoring and Evaluation Officer at EnterpriseWorks Benin (NGO funded by USAID), and Project Manager for the Renewable Energies and Environment Group – Geres (France) – CIADIC (Benin).

Dr. Chadare has coordinated several significant projects, including the “Food fortification using baobab pulp and moringa leaf powder” funded by Bill Gates/RUFORUM, and the “WEPFOOD” project funded by the Global Development Network. She has been involved in numerous research initiatives focusing on food and nutritional security, biodiversity, and sustainable agricultural practices in West Africa.

She reads, writes, and speaks French.

name: Prof. Nicolas Barro
bio:
PROF. NICOLAS BARRO represents Burkina Faso on the WASCAL Governing Board. He holds a PhD in Biochemistry-Microbiology/Virology, master’s degrees in Biochemistry-Microbiology/Virology and Biochemistry-Microbiology, a bachelor’s degree in Biological Sciences, a diploma in Plant Biotechnology from FUSAGx (Belgium), and certificates in Microbial Biotechnology and Genetic Manipulation from CNRS Marseille (France) and Public Health Management from IANPHI Helsinki (Finland).

Currently, he is the Director General of the National Biosafety Agency of Burkina Faso and a Professor at CAMES Universities. Previously, he served as President of Norbert ZONGO University, Vice-president for teaching and pedagogical innovation at Joseph KI-ZERBO University, and Deputy Director of the UFR Life and Earth Sciences at Joseph KI-ZERBO University. He also chaired the Steering Committee of the Research Network on Diseases with Epidemic Potential in Africa (REMENTA).

Prof. Barro has chaired the Board of Directors of Université Norbert ZONGO and directed the Laboratory for Epidemiology and Surveillance of Viruses and Bacteria Transmissible through Water and Food (LabESTA). He has held various academic positions in Biochemistry-Microbiology/Virology at CAMES Universities and Université Ouaga I Pr Joseph KI-ZERBO, Burkina Faso.

His international contributions include memberships in the FAO group of experts on food hygiene, the Global Foodborne Network (GFN-WHO), and the WHO-AGISAR Group on zoonoses and antibacterial resistance. He has served as an expert for the EU, NEPAD, and NGOs, and held evaluative roles for the International Science Foundation (ISF) and the CDC Atlanta. Prof. Barro is fluent in French and English.

name: Prof. Chinedum Uzoma Nwajiuba
bio:
Professor Chinedum Uzoma Nwajiuba is the chair of the WASCAL Governing Board and Nigeria’s representative on the Board. He holds a PhD, a master’s degree, and a bachelor’s degree in Agricultural Economics, as well as a master’s degree in Development Economics from Imo State University, Owerri.

Currently, he is a Professor of Agricultural Economics and the Vice-Chancellor of Alex Ekwueme Federal University Ndufu-Alike, Ikwo, Ebonyi State, Nigeria. He began his academic career at Michael Okpara University of Agriculture, Umudike, in the 1995/1996 session. He served as Dean of the School of Postgraduate Studies at Imo State University from 2011 to February 2016, and held roles such as Head of the Department of Agricultural Economics, Director of Information and Communication Technology, and Director of Academic Planning.

Professor Nwajiuba has been involved in various capacities at the Imo State University Teaching Hospital and has worked as an Adjunct Lecturer, External Examiner, and assessor for professorial promotions. He served as Executive Director of the Nigerian Environmental Study Action Team (NEST) and coordinated the Building Nigeria’s Response to Climate Change (BNRCC) project, collaborating with the Federal Ministry of Environment. He was part of the Federal Government’s team at the UNFCCC Conference of Parties and a delegate to the 2014 National Conference. He has also served on the Board of the National Agricultural Seeds Council.

His recent work includes assessments of Nigeria’s green economy, and climate-smart agriculture in Nigeria, Cameroon, and the Democratic Republic of Congo. He is an Associate Editor and Reviewer for multiple academic journals.

Professor Nwajiuba speaks English, German, and fair French.

name: Dr. Francis Boateng Agyenim
bio:
Dr. Francis Boateng Agyenim is the 2nd Vice Chair and the representative of Ghana on the WASCAL Governing Board. He holds a PhD in Solar Energy Engineering (UK), a master’s degree in Energy Conversion and Management (Germany), and a bachelor’s degree in Metallurgical Engineering (Ghana).

Currently, Dr. Agyenim is the Director of the CSIR-Institute of Industrial Research (CSIR-IIR) in Ghana. He oversees the daily administration of Ghana’s leading industrial research and development institute, which aims to drive national development and global competitiveness through scientific and technological research.

Previously, Dr. Agyenim served as the Dean of the Graduate School at Ghana Technology University College (GTUC) and held academic positions at Cardiff, Ulster, and Nottingham Universities in the UK. He has consulted on sustainable energy projects and supervised the installation of numerous solar PV systems in Ghana and Germany. Over the past five years, he has trained more than 2,600 professional electrical engineers/electricians in solar system installation and maintenance.

Dr. Agyenim serves on several university and management boards, including the University for Development Studies (UDS) Council, Ghana Nuts Management Board, National Biosafety Authority Management Board, Nursing and Midwifery Council Management Board, and CSIR Boards (Food Research Institute and Institute of Industrial Research).

He has developed and implemented the Zero Waste Disposal (ZeWaD) concept and the Industrial Innovation Hub (i2-Hub). His published works include peer-reviewed articles on renewable and alternative energies and guidelines for integrating solar-powered absorption cooling systems into buildings.

As Director of CSIR-IIR, he has significantly increased the institute’s annual internally generated fund (IGF). Dr. Agyenim has also led numerous research and development projects, contributing to Ghana’s climate targets and renewable energy initiatives.

He reads, writes, and speaks English.

name: Member Countries
bio:
Dr. Moumini Savadogo, the WASCAL Executive Director is a leader, manager and Scientist in Environment and Sustainable Development. He is also the chair of the West African technical committee for the development of the Atlas of Green hydrogen potentials.

Until his appointment as WASCAL Executive Director in 2018, Dr. Savadogo worked as Head of Burkina Faso office of the International Union for Conservation of Nature and natural resources (IUCN).

He also worked for the national Institute of Environment and Agricultural Research (INERA), the Joint Sahelian Programme of Wageningen University and the University of Ouagadougou in Burkina Faso, the regional coordinator of the W-Arly-Pendjari Programme (Benin, Burkina Faso, Niger), as well as consultant for several international and national organizations.

He has an excellent knowledge of national and regional policies and strategies on energy, agriculture, ecosystem management, poverty reduction and sustainable development, climate change as well as international agreements on environment.

Dr. Savadogo possesses rich working experience with more than 25 years in several West African countries and very familiar with multicultural and multidisciplinary teamwork. He holds a PhD in Animal Sciences/Sustainable Land Use Wageningen University, the Netherlands.

name: Prof. Daouda Kone
bio:
Professor Daouda Kone is the WASCAL Capacity Building Director since 6th January 2020.

As the head of the Capacity Building Department, he provides scientific and academic leadership and management of the different Capacity Building Programmes and, in collaboration with the Director of Research, develop work plans for the Capacity Building Department to fulfill the objectives of WASCAL. He also manages and coordinates the Capacity Building Programmes of WASCAL from the Headquarters by developing strategies to ensure effective achievement of the organization’s vision and scientific objectives.

Professor Kone additionally, oversees the capacity needs assessments of the Graduate Schools and give direction for improvement as well as build a strong network among the lead universities in the region and with WASCAL partners in overseas.

He joined WASCAL with more than 21 years as a lecturer at different stages, managing local, national, regional and international projects.

Until his appointment, he served as the Director of Graduate Studies Programme (GSP) of WASCAL Climate Change and Biodiversity since October 2012. He has also been a Full Professor in Plant Physiology at the Department of Biological Sciences, University of Cocody- Abidjan.

He played the leading role in the establishment of the GSP in Côte d’Ivoire as Centre of Excellence of World Bank in Climate Change Biodiversity and Sustainable Agriculture in 2015. He also led the establishment of two regional Master programmes linked to the GRP WASCAL for Capacity Building in Climate Change in West Africa; 17 African nationalities are hosted in this programme.

Professor Kone also worked on ensuring the international accreditation of WASCAL PhD curricula and Three (3) others by High Council for the Evaluation of Research and Higher Education (HECERES). He acted as the lead connection of Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny and Côte d’Ivoire Universities to the Regional Universities Forum for Capacity Building in Agriculture, (RUFORUM).

Professor Kone obtained his master’s in plant Physiology degree in 1991 and went on to pursue a first Doctoral Degree in Agro-physiology and Plant Pathology in 1998. He further went on to obtain a second Doctoral Degree in 2008 also in the same field from the University of Cocody-Abidjan in Côte d’Ivoire..

name: Member Countries
bio:
Prof. Kehinde Olufunso Ogunjobi is the Deputy and Research Director of the WASCAL Competence centre in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.

He holds a Ph.D. in Environmental Science and Engineering, with a focus on climate change and sustainable development.

Prof. Ogunjobi is a member of Nigeria Meteorological Society, Korea Meteorological Society, Solar Energy society of Nigeria, Society of Environmental Engineers, and Physics Society of Nigeria.

Before joining WASCAL, he was a distinguished academic and research leader in the field of climate and environmental sciences, the Head of Department, Meteorology and Climate science at the Federal University of Technology Akure (FUTA) Nigeria, the Director of WASCAL Graduate study programme on West African Climate Systems, FUTA. He was also a Fellow of the International Centre for Theoretical Physics, Trieste, Italy, and of the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation, Germany.

He has garnered extensive experience in interdisciplinary research, integrating environmental science, policy, and socio-economic aspects to address pressing issues related to climate change and land use in West Africa.

His research interests span across various domains, including Climate modeling and impact assessment, renewable energy and sustainable resource management, adaptation strategies for climate change, and policy development for environmental sustainability.

Under his leadership, the WASCAL Competence Centre has become a hub for cutting-edge research and training in climate science and land use adaptation. He has successfully spearheaded collaborations with various universities, research institutions, and governmental bodies, fostering a robust network for knowledge exchange and capacity building.

He has published more than 80 articles in reputable journals https://www.researchgate.net/search/publication?q=ogunjobi+kehinde+Olufunso, and has been a key contributor to several high-impact research projects funded by international organizations and governments of Germany (BMBF), EU, Nigeria, and Burkina Faso.

He reads, writes and speaks English language Fluently and very intermediate in French.

name: Prof. Moussa Djire
bio:
Dr. Moussa Djiré represents Mali on the WASCAL Governing Board. He holds a PhD in the History of International Relations and Foreign Policy, a master’s degree in International Relations, and diplomas in Philo-Languages series (PLA), Quality Assurance in Higher Education, socio-legal research, teaching methods, and decentralization and management of local public services.

Currently serving as Rector of the Bamako University of Legal and Political Sciences, Dr. Djiré is a lecturer specializing in International Development Law, Environmental Law, and Land Law. Over the past two decades, he has focused his research on land law, natural resource management, local governance, and institutional development, publishing extensively in these areas.

In addition to his academic role, Dr. Djiré works as an independent consultant with significant experience collaborating with international organizations such as FAO, the World Bank, IIED, and various multilateral and bilateral cooperation bodies. He has conducted numerous studies in Mali and across the sub-region.

Dr. Djiré’s past roles include Regional Coordinator for the international action research programme “Innovative Tools for Securing Land Tenure in West Africa” (funded by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation), Coordinator of the EU-funded WOSCAP Mali team, and member of the FAO group of experts developing the ECOWAS regional irrigation policy and strategy.

He is fluent in French and has fair proficiency in English and Russian.

name: Hon. Dr. Fatou Faye
bio:
Honourable Fatou Lamin Faye is the representative of The Gambia on the WASCAL Governing board.

She holds a master’s degree of Education in Management and Vocational Education, a degree in vocational Education in Developing Countries, and a diploma in Social Development.

She served the Gambian Government first as Minister of Education and then as Minister of Basic and Secondary Education.

Before that, she served as Director of the Gambia Technical Training Institute (GTTI) . She also served in a number of Boards of Governors and Committees, including The Gambian University Senate, project steering committee of the Community Skills Improvement Project (CSIP), the West African Examination Council, the international examination council, The NGO Affairs Agency Board, National Training Authority Board, Chairperson, National Women’s Council, and the ECOWAS Gender Technical Commission.

She speaks, English, Wollof, and Mandinka.

name: Mrs. Harriet Apoley Baffoe
bio:
Harriet Apoley Baffoe is a Project Management Specialist. She holds a master’s degree in project management from the Graduate school of Paris and two bachelor’s degrees: one in Business Administration and the other in Bachelor of Laws from Green Hills College, Ghana Institute of Management Studies and Wisconsin University College respectively.

She has over 25 years work experience in administration with various international organizations across the West African Sub region.

Harriet Baffoe joined WASCAL in April 2014 as an office Manager and Secretary to the WASCAL Governing Board. She served in this position for four years and rose through the ranks to her current position as Senior Administrative Manager. In her current position, she streamlined the organization administration processes by redesigning all administrative related forms and processes, she was instrumental in advocating for the establishment of the WASCAL Shared Point where both internal and external stakeholders could easily access non classified WASCAL working documents thereby reducing the use of paper to reflect the main core objective of WASCAL.

Harriet A. Baffoe is a good communicator and event planner, she speaks and write fluent English and French and speaks Eight other dialects of the West African Sub-Region.

name: Francis Jean Sempore
bio:
Principal Energy Expert, Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Specialist, Mr. Francis SEMPORE capitalizes on a professional experience of nearly thirty (30) years with to his credit the coordination, supervision and/or design of about fifty (50) programs and projects in the fields of Sustainable Energy, Resource Mobilization, Climate Finance, Capacity Building and Entrepreneurship in West Africa.

Mr. Francis SEMPORE held important positions of responsibility including the position of Executive Director of the ECOWAS Centre for Renewable Energies and Energy Efficiency (ECREEE) in Praia (Cabo Verde). Prior to joining the ECREEE, Mr. Francis SEMPORE worked for the West African Power Pool (WAPP) based in Cotonou (Benin), as Program Officer. Previously, he served for nearly twenty years at the International Institute for Water and Environmental Engineering (2iE Institute) in Ouagadougou (Burkina Faso) in several positions of responsibility, including Advisor to the General Director and Business Unit Director. Before joining the 2iE Institute, Mr. SEMPORE worked in the private sector in Abidjan (Côte d’Ivoire) and Dakar (Senegal) as Studies Engineer, Business Engineer and Country Agency Manager.

Mr. SEMPORE is an Electrical Engineer graduated from “Ecole Superieure Polytechnique – ESP” of Dakar (Senegal) and holds a Specialized Master’s Degree in Energy and Industrial Refrigeration Engineering of 2iE Institute (Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso). He is certified in Business Management from HEC Paris (France) and has a Post Master Degree in Regulation of Energy from Mines Paris Tech (France).

With the support of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), Mr. SEMPORE has just concluded the development mission of the African Energy Efficiency Facility (AfEEF) Business Case and Investment Plan as Consultant (Team Lead) for the African Energy Commission (AFREC), a specialized agency of the African Union.

Francis SEMPORE,

Expert Senior Energie, Specialiste Energies Renouvelables & Efficacité Energétique

Expert Senior en Energie, Spécialiste en Energies Renouvelables et Efficacité Energétique, M. Francis SEMPORE capitalise une expérience professionnelle de près d’une trentaine (30) d’années avec à son actif la coordination, la supervision et/ou la conception d’environ une cinquantaine (50) de programmes et de projets dans les domaines de l’Accès à l’Energie, des Energies renouvelables, de l’Efficacité Energétique, des Politiques Energétiques, du Financement Vert, de l’Intégration du Genre dans l’Energie, de l’Electrification Rurale, de la Cuisson Propre, de la Mobilité Electrique, de l’Hydrogène Vert ainsi que de l’Entrepreneuriat et du Renforcement des capacités en Afrique de l’Ouest et en Afrique du Centre.

  1. Francis SEMPORE a occupé d’importants postes de responsabilité dont la fonction de Directeur Exécutif du Centre pour les Energies Renouvelables et l’Efficacité Energétique de la CEDEAO (CEREEC/ECREEE) de Juillet 2022 à Septembre 2025 à Praia (Cabo Verde). A ce titre, il a piloté la mise en œuvre des Politiques Régionales d’Energie Durable (Energies Renouvelables, Efficacité Energétique, Bioénergie, Intégration du Genre dans l’Accès à l’Energie, Hydrogène Vert) ainsi que le développement de la Politique Régionale de Mobilité Electrique, la consolidation du Système Régional de Certification des Compétences en Energie Durable, l’Elaboration de la Facilité sur les Energies Renouvelables et l’Efficacité de la CEDEAO (EREEEF) ainsi que la Mobilisation de ressources auprès des Partenaires Techniques et Financiers pour la mise en oeuvre d’infrastructures d’énergie durable. Il a occupé également la fonction de Représentant Résident par intérim de la CEDEAO au Cap Vert sur la période d’aout 2024 à septembre 2025.

Avant de rejoinder le CEREEC, il a été Chargé de Programme au sein du Système d’Echanges d’Energie Electrique Ouest Africain (WAPP) basé à Cotonou (Bénin). Auparavant, M. SEMPORE a passé près d’une vingtaine d’a l’Institut International d’Ingénierie de l’Eau et de l’Environnement (Institut 2iE) à Ouagadougou (Burkina Faso) avec plusieurs postes de responsabilité occupés (Conseiller du Directeur Général en charge du Développement Institutionnel, de la Prospective et du Numérique, Directeur du Technopole, Directeur des Relations Internationales, Directeur de la Formation Continue et à Distance, Directeur du e-Education Center, Responsable de la formation de Master spécialisé en Génie Energétique). Avant de rejoindre l’Institut 2iE, il a travaillé dans le secteur privé dans les domaines de l’Energie, du Conditionnement d’Air et du Froid Industriel à Abidjan (Côte d’Ivoire) et à Dakar (Sénégal). Il y a occupé les fonctions d’Ingénieur d’Etudes, d’Ingénieur d’Affaires et de Responsable d’Agence Pays.

Francis SEMPORE est Ingénieur en Génie Electrique de l’Ecole Supérieure Polytechnique (ESP) de Dakar (Sénégal) et est titulaire d’un Master Spécialisé en Génie Energétique et Froid Industriel de l’Institut International d’Ingénierie de l’Eau et de l’Environnement (Institut 2iE) de Ouagadougou (Burkina Faso). Il est Certifié en Management d’Entreprise de HEC Paris et possède un Diplôme de formation spécialisée en Régulation et Marché de l’Energie de Mines ParisTech (France).

Contacts: WhatsApp: +226 7026 8478; Email: sempore.francis@gmail.com

Francis SEMPORE,

Expert Senior Energia, Especialista em Energias Renováveis & Eficiência Energética

Especialista Sênior em Energia, Especialista em Energias Renováveis e Eficiência Energética, o Sr. Francis SEMPORE capitaliza uma experiência profissional de quase trinta (30) anos com a coordenação, supervisão e/ ou concepção de cerca de cinquenta (50) de programas e projetos nos domínios do Acesso à Energia, das Energias Renováveis, da Eficiência Energética, das Políticas Energéticas, do Financiamento Verde, da Integração do Género na Energia, da Electrificação Rural, da Cozinha Limpa, da Mobilidade Eléctrica, Hidrogénio Verde e Empreendedorismo e Desenvolvimento de Capacidades na África Ocidental e Central.

O Sr. Francis SEMPORE ocupou importantes cargos de responsabilidade, incluindo a função de Diretor Executivo do Centro para as Energias Renováveis e a Eficiência Energética da CEDEAO (CEREEC/ECREEE) de Julho de 2022 a Setembro de 2025 em Praia (Cabo Verde). A este título, liderou a implementação das Políticas Regionais de Energia Sustentável (Energias Renováveis, Eficiência Energética, Bioenergia, Integração do Género no Acesso à Energia, Hidrogénio Verde) bem como o desenvolvimento da Política Regional de Mobilidade Eléctrica, a consolidação do Sistema Regional de Certificação das Competências em Energia Sustentável, a Elaboração da Facilidade sobre as Energias Renováveis e a Eficiência da CEDEAO (EREEEF) assim como a Mobilização de recursos junto dos Parceiros Técnicos e Financeiros para a implementação de infraestruturas de energia sustentável. Exerceu também a função de Representante Residente interino da CEDEAO em Cabo Verde no período de agosto de 2024 a setembro de 2025.

Antes de se juntar ao CEREEC como Director Executivo, foi Responsável de Programa no West Africa Power Pool (WAPP) sediado em Cotonou (Benim). Anteriormente, o Sr. SEMPORE passou quase vinte anos no Instituto Internacional de Engenharia da Água e do Ambiente (Instituto 2iE) em Ouagadougou (Burkina Faso) com vários cargos de responsabilidade (Assessor do Diretor Geral responsável pelo Desenvolvimento Institucional, Prospectiva e Digital, Diretor do Technopole, Diretor de Relações Internacionais, Diretor de Educação Contínua e à Distância, Diretor do Centro de Educação Electrónica, Cordenador do Mestrado especializado em Engenharia Energética). Antes de entrar para o Instituto 2iE, trabalhou no setor privado nas áreas da Energia, Ar Condicionado e Refrigeração Industrial em Abidjan (Côte d ́Ivoire) e Dakar (Senegal). Ocupou as funções de Engenheiro de Estudos, de Engenheiro de Negócios e de Responsável da Agência País.

Francis SEMPORE é Engenheiro em Engenharia Elétrica da da Escola Superior Politécnica (ESP) de Dakar (Senegal) e possui um Mestrado em Energia e Refrigeração Industrial pelo Instituto Internacional da Engenharia da Água e do Ambiente (Institut 2iE) em Ouagadougou (Burkina Faso). Tem um Certificado em Gestão de Empresas da HEC Paris e um Diploma em Regulação e Mercados Energéticos pela Mines ParisTech (França).

Contactos: WhatsApp: +226 7026 8478; Email: sempore.francis@gmail.com

name: Dr. Safiétou Sanfo
bio:
Dr. Safiétou Sanfo is an Agricultural Economist and impact analyst at the WASCAL Competence Centre.

She holds a PhD in Economics from Paris 1, Sorbonne University, France.

She coordinates the WASCAL Regional Thematic on Rural Urban and Cross Border Migration. Her research interests lie in climate change economics, adaptation strategies, and livelihoods. In recent years, she has focused on climate change, migration, impact evaluation using bio-economic and mathematical programming modeling, circular economy, governance, and institutions. Safietou Sanfo has received several research grants and professional awards, including the AVhi, the LIRA climate change and SDGs, ADA/Research Meets Africa Awards.

She has experience teaching climate change economics, Development Economics, Food security, Agricultural economics, Agri-Business, and Sustainable Development. She is the author and co-author of publications in international peer-reviewed Journals; https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=V1Y1UCoAAAAJ&hl=fr; https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Safietou-Sanfo. Safietou Sanfo is actively involved in several research and development projects on climate change-related issues. She is Associate Editor of « Emerging Science Journals, Life Science» Change and Adaptation in Socio-Ecological Systems (CASES), De Gruyter Open (April 2014 to present), and Member of the Advisory Board of the Swedish international programme of training on Climate change, mitigation, and adaptation.

She has English and French proficiency.

name: Dr. Bruno Korgo
bio:
Dr. Bruno Korgo is the Regional Coordinator of the Renewable Energy and Green Hydrogen Theme (PRT-RE) at the WASCAL Competence Centre in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. Dr. Korgo holds a PhD in Atmospheric Physics, a master’s degree in applied physics, and a master’s degree in electrical engineering and Renewable Energy.

He is responsible for coordinating and developing the renewable energy and green hydrogen theme and associated services according to the needs of ECOWAS countries. He supports the sustainable renewable energy supply strategy for West Africa, including research and development and capacity building. Dr. Korgo directly coordinates and is involved in numerous projects and initiatives in the West African region and internationally. His activities and expertise span a wide range of disciplines, including atmospheric physics, climate dynamics, climate change and energy, energy transition, energy policies, infrastructure, and innovation in renewable energy and green hydrogen technologies.

With extensive experience in research and administration in the energy sector in Burkina Faso, Dr. Korgo is an Associate Professor at the University. He has served as Director General of Renewable Energy, member and chairman of the board of the electricity utility SONABEL in Burkina Faso, and focal person for several international organisations. He has conducted several consultations as a senior energy expert for reputable organisations such as the World Bank, IFC, IRENA, and national agencies.

He has proficiency in French and English.

name: Sonia Semedo
bio:
Dr. Sónia Semedo is the Cabo Verde representative on WASCAL Governing board.

She holds a Ph.D. in Physics Engineering and an Advanced Specialisation in Biomedical Engineering from the University of Coimbra, Portugal. She also holds a master’s in physics engineering from the University of Aveiro.

She is now an Assistant Professor at University of Cape Verde, where she has been teaching since March 2016. Her current research interests are focused on the Internet of Things and Artificial Intelligence applied to water and agriculture.

Recently she won 3 scholarships: The African Research Initiative for Scientific Excellence fellowship (ARISE), Artificial Intelligence for Development of Africa (AI4D) and Fulbright Visiting Scholar to foster research at her university.

name: Prof. Ali Mahamane
bio:
Dr. Ali Mahamane represents Niger on the WASCAL Governing Board. He holds a PhD in Applied Biological Sciences with a major in Plant Biology and Ecology, a PhD in Agricultural Sciences and Biological Engineering, and a diploma in Water and Forest Engineering, specialising in Tropical Rural Forestry and Forest Management.

Currently a CAMES University Professor, Dr. Mahamane has held various academic and administrative roles, including Rector of Diffa University, Vice-Rector and Dean of the Faculty of Science and Technology at Dan Dicko Dan Koulodo University, Maradi (Niger), and Dean of the Faculty of Science and Technology at the University of Maradi. He has coordinated Niger’s participation in the Master’s degree programme in Biodiversity and Natural Resource Management, a collaboration between the University of Abomey-Calavi (Benin), Abdou Moumouni University (Niger), Free University of Brussels (Belgium), Faculty of Agronomic Sciences of Gembloux (Belgium), and the University of Liège (Belgium).

Dr. Mahamane also served as Coordinator for Niger on the UNDESERT Project (Understanding and Combating Desertification to Mitigate its Impact on Ecosystem Services).

An expert in environmental monitoring of ecosystems, he specialises in environmental impact studies of rural development projects, forest conservation, forest ecology, forest landscape management, landscape ecology, forest inventory and dendrochronology, natural forest development, rangeland and protected area management, natural resource management and conservation, plant ecology and phytosociology, protected area management evaluation, rangeland ecology, pastoral rangeland development, restoration ecology, agroforestry, biodiversity conservation, biodiversity assessment and monitoring, climate change biology, and conservation biology ecological modelling.

name: Prof. Aboudou Raoufou Pierre Radji
bio:
Prof. Pierre Raoufou Aboudou Radji is the Togolese representative on the WASCAL Governing Board. He holds a PhD in Developmental Biology, specialising in Ornamental Horticulture and Urban Ecology, and a master’s degree in Educational Sciences with a focus on the use of information and communication technologies in education and training (UTICEF).

Prof. Radji is a Professor of Plant Biology with a specialisation in Urban Ecology and Ornamental Horticulture. Previously, he was a member of the Budget Committee Governing Board of GBIF in Togo and served as Node Manager & HoD at OCDI/Caritas, and as part of the Finance and Resource Mobilization Commission. He also managed the master’s programme in Forestry and Climate Change studies at the Lab of Forest Research, EAMAU (African School of Architecture and Urban Planning). Additionally, he has been a Senior Lecturer at Togo Public Universities and the Scientific Curator at the Togo National Herbarium.

He possesses extensive skills in financial, budgeting, and accounting project management; leadership; organisational and change management; strategic business and programme development; human capital management; research and development coordination; stakeholder management; networking and communications; project design and monitoring; administration; and biodiversity informatics. His expertise extends to invasive alien species in Togo (IAS), ornamental horticulture and urban ecology, botany and plant physiology, algology, sustainable forest management, and database management.

Prof. Radji has 57 publications in 45 different journals and has been invited to numerous international conferences. He is also a reviewer and board member of various scientific journals. https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Raoufou_Radji, https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6597-8438, Researcher ID: M-8081-2013 Scopus Author ID: 56986513300

He speaks and writes in both French and English.

name: Prof. Emmanuel Ramde
bio:
Ing. Professor Emmanuel Wendsongré Ramdé is the Executive Director of the West African Science Service Centre on Climate Change and Adapted Land Use (WASCAL). He is a mechanical engineer, an energy and climate change specialist and project management, monitoring and evaluation expert. He also holds a Master’s in Business Administration (MBA), Finance option. He is a past director of The Brew-Hammond Energy Centre, Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Kumasi, Ghana and has also served as Team Leader in a number of programmes/projects such as the European Union funded programme “Improving Governance of the Energy Sector in West Africa (AGoSE-AO, acronym in French) at the ECOWAS Commission (Economic Community of West African States) and the European Union funded project for the development of the Renewable Energy Atlas of Benin Republic.

He reads, writes and speaks both English and French fluently in addition to his mother tongue, Mooré.

Ing. Professor Ramdé has about twenty years of experience in designing, implementing, managing, monitoring and evaluating energy related and climate change projects. He has been working with all the major regional and international development partners and national stakeholders including ECOWAS, UNIDO, USAID, GIZ, KfW, BMBF in Germany, AFREC, ECREEE through the Brew-Hammond Energy Centre and Arthur Energy Advisors, The World Bank through Danish Energy Management, the European Commission through AETS and NTU International A/S, etc..

He has been teaching, consulting and conducting research in Energy including Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency, global warming and climate change, Thermodynamics, Fluid Mechanics, Heat transfer, Refrigeration and Air Conditioning, Internal Combustion Engines, Turbo-machinery, Aerodynamics, Pneumatics and Hydraulics. He is also serving as visiting scholar, moderator of programmes, external examiner and scientific board member in a number of universities within and outside Ghana. He is a reviewer in a number of journals including Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews, African Journal of Science, Technology, Innovation and Development and British Journal of Applied Technologies.

In November 2020, Ing. Professor Ramdé was made “Chevalier de l’Ordre de l’Etalon’’ (Knight of the Order of the Stallion), the highest national award of Burkina Faso conferred to people by the president for outstanding personal merit and distinguished service to the nation.

name: Sié Sylvestre Da
bio:
Sié Sylvestre Da is a senior scientist at the WASCAL Competence Centre and coordinator of the regional Experts Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services for the CABES project. He holds a PhD in Botany from the University of Bonn, Germany. He has extensive experience facilitating dialogue between biodiversity and ecosystem experts from universities, research institutions, science-policy interfaces, decision-makers, and practitioners across Africa.

His research focuses on the spatial patterns of plant biodiversity in West Africa and their implications for conservation. He investigates trends in the distribution of biodiversity in the region under the impact of climate change and land use intensification.

Dr. Da contributed to the establishment of the Red List of Ecosystems in five catchments in West and Central Africa, aiming for sustainable management of resources in these areas as part of the PREE project, implemented in collaboration with the IUCN.

He has proficiency in French, English, and German.

name: Dr. Belko Abdoul-Aziz Diallo
bio:
Dr. Belko Abdoul-Aziz Diallo is a Computer Science Engineer and a Geomatics Scientist. He is a practitioner and researcher in Data Management and Data Science at WASCAL. He holds a PhD in Geomatics, Geospatial, and Geo-Informatics sciences and technologies.

Dr. Diallo joined WASCAL in May 2016 as a Senior Data Manager and Head of IT. In 2020, he was appointed Data Management Scientist and Head of the Data Management Department (DMD). In this role, he has significantly enhanced Data, Science, and Technology units, including climate observation systems, GIS and Remote Sensing, and High-Performance Computing. He has also expanded the department to incorporate technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, the Internet of Things (IoT), and the establishment of an AIoT FabLab. This FabLab aims to develop affordable, high-quality smart devices for climate observation, smart agriculture, health, renewable energy, and climate change adaptation solutions.

The Data Management Department, under his leadership, comprises of a dozen staff members and six units, including Observation Networks, GIS and Remote Sensing Lab, IT and High-Performance Computing, Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things, and Data Governance and Management. He is the lead administrator of the WASCAL Open Data Infrastructure (WADI).

He serves on the scientific board of WASCAL Graduate School on Informatics for Climate Change in Ouagadougou and is an associate lecturer. He is a trained drone pilot and a Google-trained Machine Learning Engineer.

He speaks and writes French, English, and basic Arabic.

name: Dr. Kwame Oppong Hackman
bio:
Dr. Kwame Oppong Hackman is a senior scientist at WASCAL, and coordinates research and project implementation activities related to the Priority Research Theme 1 (land use, land cover, and land degradation) in West Africa.

He holds a PhD in Ecology, an MSc in GIS and Environmental Modelling, as well as a Postgraduate Diploma and a BSc, both in Mathematics.

Prior to his current role, he was a GIS and Remote Sensing Scientist at WASCAL Competence Centre (Burkina Faso), lecturer at the University of Energy and Natural Resources (Ghana), and a research scientist at the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (Ghana).

He is a trained ecologist with about ten years of work experience in teaching and research as well as project implementation and services development in West Africa (mainly Ghana and Burkina Faso) particularly in fields related to remote sensing, GIS, and land management where he has published widely in highly reputed scientific journals (See Google Scholar for details). Currently, he coordinates two WRAP2.0 projects (LANDSURF and CONCERT), two other BMBF-funded projects (DecLaRe and COINS), and two third-party projects (PPeDMaS and iGST) which cover fields such as sustainable land use management, environmental monitoring and assessment, precision agriculture, and climate governance.

He has English proficiency and speaks basic French.

name: Dr. Seyni Salack

memberships.name: Dr. Seyni Salack

role: Ag. DIRECTOR OF RESEARCH COMPETENCE CENTRE
bio:
Dr. Seyni Salack is a Senior Research Scientist and the Regional Thematic Coordinator on Risks and vulnerability to climate extremes at the WASCAL Competence Centre in Burkina-Faso. He holds a PhD in climate and climatic impacts, and a master’s in Atmospheric Physics – Atmospheric, Oceanography and management of semi-aris areas.

Before joining WASCAL, he was a visiting research associate at the International Research Institute, IRI/Earth Institute of the Columbia University (USA). He gained great experiences from the AGRHYMET Regional Centre (Niger), and the Institute of Meteorology and Climate Research, Atmospheric Environmental Research of the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (Germany).

He has more than eighteen years of work experience in various climate adaptation, environment, and resilience projects, research & climate services, training & capacity building, and consultancy jobs in Africa. His fields of expertise include Multihazard Risk information, Multihazard early warning systems, anticipatory action and disaster risk reduction, climate variability & energy management nexus, near-surface weather/climate observation systems, rainfall estimation using microwave links, agricultural meteorology research and extensions, verification of numerical weather predictions, seasonal-to-sub-seasonal forecasts, and statistical methods in climate data analysis. He is the author and co-author of many publications in international peer-reviewed journals (https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=8zl00asAAAAJ), hundreds of conference talks, university lectureship, two Atlases (on the Sahel, Benin & Niger) and reviewer of many students’ theses (https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Seyni_Salack).

He has developed several projects funded and implemented under his technical and managerial scrutiny between 2016 and 2021 including APTE-21 project (budget: €230,000; 2016-2018, IRD/MAEA), Co-PI for CIREG project (“Climate Information for Renewable Energy Generation”, leader of Work Package 2, budget for WP2: €505,800; 2018-2021; funding from ERA4CS/BMBF) and PI & Lead Coordinator for UPSCALERS project (“UPscaling Site-Specific Climate-smart Agriculture and Land-use practices to Enhance Regional Production Systems in West-Africa”, budget: $1,197,000; AUC, Research Grant No AURG II-1074-2016, 2018-2021), the I-CHANGE project (“Individual Change of HAbits Needed for Green European transition”, budget: 4.9 million Euro, EUC/EUH2020, 2021-2025), and the Network of Centres of Excellence in Disaster Risk Reduction (NoE, budget: 1.400,000 USD, UNDRR, 2023 & 2024).

He has proficiency in French, English, and Arabic.

name: Ass. Prof. MOUNKAILA SALEY Moussa
bio:
Dr. Mounkaila Saley Moussa is the Coordinator of the International Master Programme in Energy and Green Hydrogen (IMP-EGH) at WASCAL Headquarters in Accra, Ghana. In this role, he builds a robust communication environment among stakeholders and partners, drives the programme’s academic excellence, and develops the strategic partnerships that underpin its long-term sustainability, working closely with the Capacity Building Department and the Regional Coordination for Renewable Energy and Green Hydrogen.

Dr. Mounkaila holds a PhD in Meteorology and Climate Science, completed through the WASCAL Graduate Research Program in West African Climate Systems at the Federal University of Technology Akure, Nigeria. His academic path also includes an Erasmus Mundus MSc in Materials and Sensor Systems for Environmental Technologies (University of Bologna, Italy, and KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Sweden), a Professional master’s in electrical engineering from Cheikh Anta Diop University and MSc in Physics option Renewable Energy from Abdou Moumouni University (UAM), Niamey.

Dr. Mounkaila is an Associate Professor at UAM in Niamey, Niger, where he has also served as Deputy Head of the Physics Department Faculty of Science, and has held interim leadership roles as Director of the IMP-EGH programme and Scientific Coordinator at WASCAL’s Doctoral Research Programme on Climate Change and Energy (DRP-CCE) in Niger. He has over a decade of experience designing, implementing and supervising research and academic programmes in climate science and renewable energy at UAM. He has worked on projects funded by major international partners including the European Union (through the EU/Horizon 2020), the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD), BMBF and USAID. He had been a visiting scientist at the University of Cape Town’s Climate System Analysis Group.

Dr. Mounkaila has been teaching, supervising and conducting research in Climate Science, Atmospheric Physics, Renewable Energy and Green hydrogen, Climate Modelling, and Energy Economics, at both undergraduate and graduate levels, including Master’s and PhD supervision. He has authored or co-authored many peer-reviewed publications in international journals including Energy Reports, Energies, Atmospheric Research, Environmental Research Letters, and Theoretical and Applied Climatology.

He was awarded the WASCAL PhD Scholarship (2012–2015), the European Union’s Erasmus Mundus Scholarship for Third Country students (2009–2011), and the Agence Universitaire de la Francophonie (AUF) scholarship (2006–2008).

He reads, writes and speaks both French and English fluently.

name: Prof. Benjamin L LAMPTEY
bio:
Benjamin Lamptey is a Visiting Professor of meteorology at the University of Leeds. He was a lead author of the Working Group 1 of the Sixth Assessment Report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) AR6 WG1 (released in August 2021).
He is a Guest Editor of Special Issues for the Frontiers in Environmental Science; MDPIAtmosphere Journals respectively; an Editorial Board member of the Environmental Research – Climate Journal and was an Associate Editor of the Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society (2020 to 2024).
He serves on the Scientific Advisory Committees of the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA) Climate Research for Development in Africa (CR4D) and that of the West African Science Service Centre for Climate Change and Adapted Land Use (WASCAL). He
served on the World Climate Research Programme (WCRP) Task Force on Coordinated Regional Downscaling Experiment (CORDEX) (2010-2012); Scientific Steering group of the WCRP Global Energy and Water Exchanges (GEWEX) (2021 -2025); Member of Working Group on African Monsoon of the WCRP
Monsoon Panel (2021-205); Scientific Steering Committee of the WMO World Weather Research Programme (WWRP) (2014 – 2018); Cochair of the WMO World Weather Research Programme THORPEX (2009 – 2014).
In 2013, he joined the African Centre of Meteorological Applications for Development (ACMAD) in Niamey, Niger as the Deputy Director-General (DDG) and became the Acting Director General cumulatively with the DDG position for two years (1st January 2017 to 31st December 2018), before joining the University of Leeds, UK, as a Cheney Fellow in 2019. Prior to joining ACMAD, he was the Acting Dean of the School of Graduate Studies cumulatively with being Acting Head of the Nautical Science Department at the Regional Maritime University in Accra, Ghana. He was a postdoctoral fellow at the National Center for Atmospheric Research
(NCAR) in Boulder, Colorado USA from 2005 to 2007 where he run the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) Model in both weather and climate modes. He also run the NCAR Community Land Model (CLM) in offline model. He started his meteorology career as a Weather Forecaster at the Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet), having been trained at the UK Meteorological Office College in Shinfield Park, Reading and later
became the Head of the Climatology Division of GMet. He led the computerization of the national climatological records.
He lectures part-time and supervises Graduate students in various African Universities. These include universities within the West African Science Service Centre for Climate Change and Adapted Land Use (WASCAL) Programme, African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS), Pan African University for Water and Energy Science, including Climate Change (PAUWES), University of Ghana, University of Cape Coast, Kwame
Nkrumah University of Science and Technology and the University College of Agriculture and
Environmental Studies.

He serves as external examiner to graduate theses in universities in Europe and Africa. He holds a PhD in Geosciences (with minor in High Performance Computing) (run both the GENESIS Global Climate Model and MM5 Regional Climate Model) and an MSc in Meteorology (run the RegCM Regional Climate Model), both from the Pennsylvania State University, USA. In addition, he possesses an MSc in Applied and Agricultural Meteorology (University of Reading, UK); University of Oxford Delegacy of Local Examinations Diploma in
Computing and Information Systems, (London College of Business and Computing, UK); Certificate in Weather Forecasting (UK Meteorological Office College) and BSc (Hons) Physics from the Kwame Nkrumah University of
Science and Technology, Kumasi Ghana.
HONORS
Elected to Meteorology Honor Society of Chi Epsilon Pi, for demonstrated interest and ability in meteorology – October 1998 Certificate of Honor for dedicated services during National Service (teaching Physics) at Sunyani Secondary School, Ghana – December 1985
